title: Unramified algebraic-space morphisms: base change, composition and cancellation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $X,Y,Z$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For morphisms $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$, if both are unramified, then $g\circ f$ is unramified; if $g\circ f$ is unramified, then $f$ is unramified, with no condition on $g$. Every base change of an unramified morphism of algebraic spaces is unramified. Every etale morphism of algebraic spaces is unramified. Unramified means locally of finite type with the scheme notion [def-weil-unramified-morphism] on etale scheme charts; etale uses [def-weil-etale-morphism] on charts.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $c:W\to Z$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] to $g$ with prescribed target atlas $W$: obtain a surjective etale atlas $b:V\to Y$ and $v:V\to W$ with $cv=gb$. Apply it again to $f$ with target atlas $V$: obtain a surjective etale atlas $a:U\to X$ and $u:U\to V$ with $bu=fa$. Thus $cvu=gfa$, so $U\to W$ is also a compatible chart diagram for $gf$.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ and $g$ are unramified. The chart-recognition equivalence [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] makes $u$ and $v$ unramified scheme morphisms. Their composite $vu$ is unramified by [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-composition-cancellation]. Since $a:U\to X$ is surjective, the same chart-recognition equivalence applied to $U\to W$ shows that $gf$ is unramified.

Suppose instead that $gf$ is unramified. The compatible diagram $U\to W$ makes $vu$ unramified by [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts]. Scheme left cancellation [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-composition-cancellation] gives that $u$ is unramified without any hypothesis on $v$. Applying chart recognition to $U\to V$ gives that $f$ is unramified. In particular no condition on $g$ entered the argument.

For an arbitrary algebraic-space morphism $t:Y'\to Y$, put $P=X\times_Y Y'$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $q:Q\to Y'$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and set $V'=V\times_Y Q$ and $U'=U\times_V V'$. The products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Both are schemes: $V'$ is a scheme because $V\to Y$ is representable, and $U'$ is a scheme fibre product. The induced $b':V'\to Y'$ is the composite $V'\to Q\to Y'$, while $a':U'\to P$ identifies with the composite $U\times_Y Q\to X\times_Y Q\to P$. The identification is given on test schemes by $(x,(v,z))\mapsto(x,z)$, with inverse $(x,z)\mapsto(x,(u(x),z))$. The two composites are identities since the fibre-product relation forces $v=u(x)$. Here $V'\to Q$ is the pullback of $b$ and $Q\to Y'$ is the atlas $q$ itself. The two factors of $a'$ are pullbacks of $a$ and $q$, respectively. Thus the cover assertion of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes each pullback factor surjective etale. Their composites are representable surjective etale as well: after any scheme test map, successive fibre products are schemes, and their projections compose to the required projection; scheme etale composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] and scheme surjective composition [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition] apply. The defining equations of the fibre products give $b'h'=f'a'$ for $h':U'\to V'$ and $f':P\to Y'$.

source.place: Tag 03ZJ (lemma-base-change-unramified), expanding remark-base-change-P with scheme charts.

proof.text: If $f$ is unramified, chart recognition [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] gives that $u:U\to V$ is unramified. The morphism $h':U'=U\times_V V'\to V'$ from the preceding step is its scheme base change, hence unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open], clause (1). Since $a'$ is surjective, chart recognition in the compatible diagram $U'\to V'$ gives that $f':P\to Y'$ is unramified. The map $t$ was arbitrary.

Finally assume $f$ is etale in the chartwise sense of the statement. The compatible chart $u:U\to V$ is etale by [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts]. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], scheme etaleness includes unramifiedness, so $u$ is unramified. Since $a$ is surjective, the same chart-recognition equivalence shows $f$ is unramified.
